answer.answer: The study's check confirmed five settings on five different scenes (S6, S12, S3, S1, S7), but the triage shows that only three of them are failures of the VaVAM policy. In every confirmed case the recorded cars ran at their recorded timing. Only the speed changed: 2x on 0e899dd3 (S12), and 1.25x on 023b7fcc (S1) and 09a95ffa (S7). In these three the policy usually steered left out of its lane, against a STRAIGHT or RIGHT command, into a car beside it or ahead of it in the next lane. S12 is the clearest case, because every failure there was the policy's fault. S1 and S7 rest on a few runs each, and in each of them one failure was a replayed car coming into the ego, with fault unclear. The other two confirmed cases, S6 (096988dd at 2x) and S3 (054b5901 at 1.5x), say nothing about the policy. In every run there, a sped-up replayed car came from behind and drove through the ego before handoff, and the overlap was scored as a front collision. That is a rear-end hit, which the brief said to ignore, and it is an artifact of replaying faster cars rather than a challenging case.

findings.claim: On 0e899dd3, speeding the cars to 2x made the policy fail in every run. Each time it drifted left, against a STRAIGHT then RIGHT command, and ran its front into a slow car in the adjacent left lane. At 1.25x and 1.5x the same scene passed, though with high criticality, so the speed-up is what breaks it. This is the strongest confirmed policy failure.

On 023b7fcc at 1.25x, every run failed. In most of them the policy made an unprompted left lane change and sped up into a car driving alongside it. In one run that car cut across into the ego's path, and fault there is unclear.

On 09a95ffa at 1.25x, every run failed. In one the policy drifted left into a car passing in the adjacent lane. In the other the replayed car came up from behind on the left and struck the ego, with fault unclear. This case rests on very few runs.

The confirmed cases on 096988dd at 2x and 054b5901 at 1.5x are not policy failures. In every run a sped-up replayed car hit the ego from behind and drove through it while the ego was still replaying the log. The overlap was scored as a front collision at the moment of handoff. These are rear-end, replay-overlap events, which the brief said to exclude. At lower speeds both scenes passed.

On 1c45ce3a at 1.25x, one run failed by leaving the road: the policy ignored a RIGHT command and drifted onto the median shoulder. The failure-rate range stays below one half, and this run is flagged as a possible simulator artifact because the ego was far off the recorded path. Triage nevertheless judged the policy at fault.

Retiming the cars earlier (by up to 1.5 s) and speeding them up on 12855a41, the one scene where timing was explored, never produced a failure, although several runs came close. On 0cf6368d and 19f339ba the few runs tried all passed.
The failures the policy caused were mostly its own left lane changes into cars in the adjacent lane, not failures to respond to another car cutting in.

open: Only three scenes have confirmed failures by the policy. The two remaining places in the top 5 need new candidates: repeat 1c45ce3a at 1.5x or 2x, and retry 12855a41, which came close at negative time shifts and high speed.
S6 and S3 should be rescored with collisions before handoff and rear-end overlaps excluded. Then probe 096988dd and 054b5901 at speeds or time shifts where replayed cars do not drive through the ego.
The cars' timing was barely explored: almost every setting used a 0 s shift. Shifts of ±1 to 2 s on the confirmed scenes (0e899dd3, 023b7fcc, 09a95ffa) would show whether timing matters.

023b7fcc and 09a95ffa were never run at 1.0x with replayed traffic. Without that, it is not shown that the 1.25x speed-up causes their failures rather than the scene itself. Run each at 1.0x a few times.
S1 and S7 rest on few runs, each with one failure of unclear fault. More repeats there would firm up both the failure rate and the share caused by the policy.
Near misses were never turned into a checked ranking, so the order among cases that did not fail is not established.
